answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet, on both counts. A classic guide after a marathon is about one easy day per race mile before hard training, which puts real speedwork around the second week of November for you. This week I want you at roughly 22 miles, all easy, adding a fifth day back. If you still feel springy next weekend, we can bring back strides, then one light session the week after.

For the Thanksgiving 10K, it is possible but I would not call it a goal race. If you want to jog it as a hard training day, fine. If you want to actually race it, tell me and I will build two short, sharp weeks into the plan after this one, but expect it to feel rougher than a fresh 10K would.

new.analysis:
You followed the recovery week exactly as planned: three easy runs on Wed, Fri and Sun at 3, 4 and 5 miles, with heart rate drifting down and pace creeping up on its own. That is the body saying the marathon is clearing, which is why you feel itchy to train. It is also why I want to resist the jump.

Two weeks is early. Your quads were wrecked eight days ago, and connective tissue takes longer to bounce back than how your legs feel on a 5-miler. Going from 12 miles with no quality to 40 miles with intervals in one step is the single most common way runners pick up a niggle in November. A smaller step now protects the bigger block that comes after.

So this week adds a fifth day and nudges the long one toward 7 miles, still all easy. Before I write anything spicier, I need to know the target. Options as I see them: race the Thanksgiving 10K and build two sharp weeks into it; use it as a tune-up jog and point at a spring half or marathon; or take a true down-cycle of easy base through November and pick a goal in December. Tell me which and I will shape next week around it.
